bracket: [Textbook misprint: the fourth alternative is printed as \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CHCl}\), whose last carbon is written \(\mathrm{CHCl}\) and so has only three bonds. It is transcribed exactly as printed. Read as the intended \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl}\) it would be 1-chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane, which is a six-carbon halide and still fails the question's own test, since reduction would give 2,3-dimethylbutane \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\) and not \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\). The answer is unaffected either way.]

[Textbook misprint: alternative d is printed as \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_3-CH_3}\), in which the third carbon is written \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) in the middle of a chain and so would carry five bonds. It is transcribed exactly as printed; the intended structure is \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3}\), 2-methylbutane. The answer is unaffected, because 2-methylbutane has no carbon bonded to four different groups and so is achiral on either reading.]
